{"status":"ok","message-type":"work","message-version":"1.0.0","message":{"indexed":{"date-parts":[[2026,11,4]],"date-time":"2026-11-04T01:56:54Z","timestamp":1793757414064,"version":"4.6.1"},"reference-count":33,"publisher":"American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS)","issue":"5203","content-domain":{"domain":[],"crossmark-restriction":false},"short-container-title":["Science"],"published-print":{"date-parts":[[1995,3,10]]},"abstract":"<jats:p>Psychophysical measurements indicate that human subjects can store approximately seven short-term memories. Physiological studies suggest that short-term memories are stored by patterns of neuronal activity. Here it is shown that activity patterns associated with multiple memories can be stored in a single neural network that exhibits nested oscillations similar to those recorded from the brain. Each memory is stored in a different high-frequency (\"40 hertz\") subcycle of a low-frequency oscillation. Memory patterns repeat on each low-frequency (5 to 12 hertz) oscillation, a repetition that relies on activity-dependent changes in membrane excitability rather than reverberatory circuits. This work suggests that brain oscillations are a timing mechanism for controlling the serial processing of short-term memories.<\/jats:p>","DOI":"10.1126\/science.7878473","type":"journal-article","created":{"date-parts":[[2006,10,27]],"date-time":"2006-10-27T18:19:42Z","timestamp":1161973182000},"page":"1512-1515","source":"Crossref","is-referenced-by-count":1272,"title":["Storage of 7 \u00b1 2 Short-Term Memories in Oscillatory Subcycles"],"prefix":"10.1126","volume":"267","author":[{"given":"John E.","family":"Lisman","sequence":"first","affiliation":[],"role":[{"vocabulary":"crossref","role":"author"}]},{"given":"Marco A.
